title: Workshop Arcade catalog manifest
description: The single source of truth for the catalog. Every generator (build-sitemap, build-feed, build-og-images, inject-game-meta) and every validator pulls from this file, so editors should validate entries against this schema while they're being edited. The contract is enforced again in CI by scripts/check-manifest-schema.mjs.

id.description: Stable lower-kebab identifier used by FALLBACK_GAMES, the player modal, and the Workshop draft store. Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$.

title.description: Display title shown on the catalog card, in the player modal header, in JSON-LD VideoGame.name, in feed.json items, and on the per-game OG share card.

subtitle.description: Short tagline (one sentence). Surfaces on the catalog card, as meta description on the per-game HTML, in the JSON-LD VideoGame.description, and in feed.json items.

items.description: Category label. Must appear in index.html's CATEGORY_ORDER for the catalog filter chip to render in the right group.

tags.description: Categories the game belongs to. Drives filter chip counts, JSON-LD VideoGame.genre, feed.json item.tags, and the OG share-card pill row.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier used in deep links (#play=<slug>), recent-plays storage, OG share-card filenames, and JSON Feed item ids. Usually matches id; differs only when the game's published title doesn't match its catalog id (e.g. Klondike Solitaire keeps id=solitaire but slug=solitaire).

url.description: Repo-relative path to the standalone game HTML file. Must live under websites/ and end with .html so validate-catalog.ps1 + smoke-games can serve it directly.

cover.description: Repo-relative path to the 640x360 catalog cover. Prefer SVG for the same dark-theme gradient the generated OG share cards use. The matching 1200x630 share card lives at covers/og/<slug>.svg and is generated by build-og-images.

addedAt.description: ISO 8601 calendar date when the game first landed in the catalog. Drives the default newest-first sort, sitemap.xml lastmod, and feed.json item.date_published.

popularity.description: Subjective ranking used by the 'Most Popular' sort. New games typically start in the 50-70 range and may climb based on play counts collected via the recent-plays surface.
